title: Bitcoin Climbs Past $65,500 as ETF Inflows and Clarity Act Progress Fuel Rally
excerpt: Five straight days of institutional inflows totaling over $600 million and a breakthrough on crypto legislation have pushed Bitcoin to its highest level in weeks, though India's punitive tax regime keeps diaspora investors on the sidelines.
body:
• Bitcoin hit a two-week high near $65,500 on Tuesday, gaining 5% over the past week as U.S. spot ETFs recorded five consecutive days of net inflows exceeding $600 million.
  • President Trump agreed to an ethics clause in the CLARITY Act, removing a key hurdle for the crypto market-structure bill before Congress's August recess.
  • India retained its 30% flat tax and 1% TDS on crypto in its 2026 budget, driving nearly three-quarters of its $6.1 billion crypto trading volume offshore.
  • Analysts project Bitcoin could rally toward $80,000–$85,000 over the next two to three months if macroeconomic conditions align.

ETF Buying Reverses Eight-Week Outflow Streak

Bitcoin rose to approximately $65,500 on Tuesday, marking its strongest level in two weeks and building on a 5% weekly gain. Around $33 billion changed hands during the session as the broader crypto market cap climbed 1.56% to $2.24 trillion.

The rally's backbone is institutional money. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs pulled in $227 million on July 20 alone, extending the buying streak to five sessions and reversing an eight-week run of net outflows that had stretched through late June. The five-day total topped $600 million — the most sustained institutional demand since mid-July. Net ETF assets rose to roughly $79.16 billion.

Derivatives activity confirmed the momentum. Bitcoin futures trading volume surged 95% to $59.67 billion, while open interest climbed 2.36% to $49.07 billion. Options volume jumped 138% to $3.25 billion.

"If the CPI data holds and the Fed signals a credible pivot path, the conditions for sustained ETF inflows are back in place."

— Nicolai Sondergaard, Research Analyst, Nansen

Clarity Act Clears a Key Hurdle in Washington

The legislative backdrop improved markedly after President Trump agreed to an ethics provision tied to the CLARITY Act, a bill that would divide digital-asset oversight between the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. An industry source told The Block the agreement was reached Monday evening, breaking months of deadlock over a clause restricting top government officials and their families from profiting on crypto while in office.

The bill still needs 60 votes in the Senate before Congress leaves for its August recess. Polymarket traders place a 41% probability on the CLARITY Act becoming law in 2026, down from a peak of 82% in mid-February. But Fundstrat's head of digital-asset strategy Sean Farrell said odds "may be better than markets appreciate," noting that advocacy groups close to the negotiations express "materially greater optimism" than prediction markets imply.

Stifel Washington policy strategist Brian Gardner pegged the bill's chances at 30%, warning the figure could fall below 20% if the Senate does not act before recess.

Macro Tailwinds and Asian Tech Rebound

Cooler-than-expected June CPI data earlier in the week fed the risk-on mood, prompting some investors to reconsider hawkish Federal Reserve expectations ahead of the July 28–29 meeting, where a rate hike is priced at just 15% odds. A tech-sector rebound in Asia added fuel: South Korea and Taiwan benchmarks each rose roughly 4%, Japan's Nikkei gained 3%, and a mainland China tech index jumped nearly 7%.

Jeff Mei, COO at crypto exchange BTSE, described current prices as "low but fair, given the macro uncertainties pervading markets." Analyst Michaël van de Poppe said Bitcoin could push toward $80,000–$85,000 over two to three months, a zone that would coincide with the 50-week moving average — a level he identifies as typical resistance in the early stage of a post-bear-market recovery.

India's Tax Wall Keeps Diaspora Investors at Bay

For the Indian diaspora, the rally is a spectator event as much as an investment opportunity. India's 2026 Union Budget left the country's crypto tax regime untouched: a flat 30% tax on digital-asset gains with no loss offsets, plus a 1% tax deducted at source on every transaction. The framework, first imposed in 2022, has driven an estimated three-quarters of India's $6.1 billion in annual crypto trading volume to offshore platforms, according to parliamentary estimates.

India's securities regulator SEBI has proposed a multi-regulator model for overseeing exchanges and token offerings, but the Reserve Bank of India remains opposed to legitimizing the sector. A long-awaited crypto policy discussion paper was blocked by the RBI earlier this year, leaving the regulatory standoff unresolved. India is expected to adopt the OECD's Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework by April 2027, which would expose offshore wallet activity to Indian tax authorities — narrowing the window for diaspora investors using foreign platforms.

With Bitcoin still down more than 27% from its October record near $126,200, the current push toward $66,000 remains a test of whether institutional flows can sustain a recovery or merely deliver another false start in a corrective year.
image_caption: Bitcoin has climbed past 5,500, driven by strong ETF inflows and progress on the CLARITY Act in Congress.
nri_angle: India's 30% flat tax and 1% TDS on crypto, left unchanged in the 2026 budget, continue to push Indian diaspora investors toward offshore platforms even as Bitcoin rallies on ETF inflows and U.S. regulatory progress.
